mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine typically costs £1,200-£3,200 supply-only, depending on power output and condition. EB2ADT 110hp units start around £1,200, while EP5/HNS 130hp units range £1,500-£3,200. Used engines start from £600. Supply & fit adds £400-£900 labour. Peugeot dealer replacement can exceed £6,500. Check Peugeot's Customer Support Programme - you may be entitled to 100% coverage.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech low oil pressure warning?

acceptedAnswer.text: The low oil pressure warning on Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engines is caused by wet timing belt degradation. The belt runs inside the engine, exposed to heat and oil, and sheds rubber particles that block the oil pump strainer, starving the engine of lubrication. Peugeot recommends belt inspection every 20,000 km or 1 year, with replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years. Peugeot's Customer Support Programme covers 100% of costs for oil pressure issues from premature timing belt degradation, up to 10 years or 112,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine is usually worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £1,200-£3,200 versus £6,000-£18,000 for a comparable used 3008. With Peugeot dealer replacement exceeding £6,500, specialist rebuilt units offer exceptional value. Check eligibility for Peugeot's Customer Support Programme - some repairs may be covered at 100% for up to 10 years / 112,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engines typically reach 100,000-150,000 miles. However, the wet belt is the critical lifespan limiter - Peugeot recommends replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years, whichever comes first. Regular oil changes with correct PSA-approved oil and belt inspections are essential for longevity. Some owners report belt failures as early as 45,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between EB2ADT and EP5/HNS engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EB2ADT is the 110hp 1.2 PureTech fitted to Access, Active and base Allure trims. The EP5/HNS (also known as EB2ADTS) is the 130hp 1.2 PureTech fitted to Allure 130, GT Line and GT trims. Both use the same 1.2L (1,199cc) three-cylinder turbocharged architecture and share the wet belt vulnerability. The 130hp variant commands a higher replacement cost due to its higher-spec calibration and turbocharger.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine code appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Common codes include EB2ADT (110hp), EP5 (130hp) and HNS (EB2ADTS) (130hp). Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech has been the dominant petrol engine across the second-generation (2016-present) 3008 range, powering everything from entry-level Access to high-spec GT and GT Line trims. Part of Stellantis's EB2 family, the 1.2 PureTech replaced older 1.6L VTi and THP units with a more efficient three-cylinder turbocharged design, delivering outputs from 110hp to 130hp. However, the engine's wet timing belt design has made it the subject of intense UK replacement demand, with Peugeot launching a Customer Support Programme covering 100% of costs for certain repairs up to 10 years or 112,000 miles.

milestones.description: **2016** - Second-generation 3008 launched with EB2ADT 1.2L PureTech 110hp (110hp) and EP5/HNS 1.2L PureTech 130hp (130hp)
**2017** - Peugeot 3008 wins European Car of the Year; PureTech becomes the default petrol engine across the range
**2018** - Minor ECU refinements to improve cold-start behaviour and fuel mapping
**2019** - Revised wet belt materials introduced to address premature degradation concerns
**2021** - Peugeot issues technical bulletin on PureTech belt inspection and revised maintenance intervals
**2024** - Stellantis launches Customer Support Programme covering 100% of costs for oil pressure issues and excessive oil consumption on PureTech 1.0 and 1.2 engines, up to 10 years or 112,000 miles

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech's EB2 engine family is the subject of intense UK replacement demand due to one critical vulnerability - the wet timing belt. Unlike conventional belts, the PureTech's belt runs inside the engine, constantly exposed to heat and engine oil. Over time, the belt degrades, shedding rubber particles that clog the oil pump strainer, triggering low oil pressure warnings and, if ignored, catastrophic engine failure. Every rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Peugeot has also launched a Customer Support Programme covering 100% of costs for certain PureTech repairs up to 10 years or 112,000 miles - check eligibility before committing.

problems.h4: Wet Belt Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 1.2 PureTech Engines Lose Oil Pressure
problems.rootCause: The wet timing belt degrades over time, shedding rubber particles into the engine oil. These particles block the oil pump strainer, starving the engine of lubrication and triggering the low oil pressure warning. Unburned fuel can also seep past the piston rings and mix with the oil, forming an abrasive mixture that accelerates belt wear. The belt typically requires replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years - but many owners report failures well before this interval.
